extraction.name: Video-MME: The First-Ever Comprehensive Evaluation Benchmark of Multi-modal LLMs in Video Analysis
extraction.description: Video-MME is a comprehensive Multi-Modal Evaluation benchmark for MLLMs in Video analysis, featuring 900 videos across 6 visual domains with 30 subfields, durations from 11 seconds to 1 hour, multi-modal inputs including subtitles and audios, and 2,700 high-quality manually annotated multiple-choice questions.
extraction.creator: Chaoyou Fu, Yuhan Dai, Yongdong Luo, Lei Li, Shuhuai Ren, Renrui Zhang, Zihan Wang, Chenyu Zhou, Yunhang Shen, Mengdan Zhang, Peixian Chen, Yanwei Li, Shaohui Lin, Sirui Zhao, Ke Li, Tong Xu, Xiawu Zheng, Enhong Chen, Caifeng Shan, Ran He, Xing Sun
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The construction involves three main steps: video collection, question-answer annotation, and quality review. Videos are collected from YouTube across 6 key domains with 30 finely-grained categories, ensuring diverse coverage. Annotators with strong English proficiency and research experience create three multiple-choice questions per video after thorough viewing. A rigorous manual review process is conducted, including examination by different annotators and filtering using Gemini 1.5 Pro to ensure questions require video content.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw videos are sourced from YouTube, with corresponding meta-information such as subtitles (if provided) and audios. The dataset consists of 900 videos, including 744 videos with subtitles and all 900 with audios.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Videos are collected with varying duration lengths: short (<2 minutes), medium (4-15 minutes), and long (30-60 minutes). Frame extraction is performed for evaluation: for Gemini 1.5 Pro, frames are sampled at 1 frame per second for short and medium videos, and 1 frame every 2 seconds for long videos; other models follow their official guidelines with specific frame counts.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators with strong English proficiency and extensive research experience in vision-language learning are recruited. Each annotator thoroughly views the entire video and iteratively creates three relevant multiple-choice questions per video, each with four candidate options, resulting in 2,700 QA pairs. Questions encompass 12 distinct task types including perception, reasoning, and information synthesis, designed to be closely tied to video content.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A rigorous manual review process is conducted: each QA pair is examined by a different annotator to verify language clarity, logical consistency, and appropriateness. Additionally, text-only questions are provided to Gemini 1.5 Pro to filter out QA pairs answerable without video content; those not meeting this criterion are returned for revision. Statistical analysis shows Gemini 1.5 Pro achieves less than 15% accuracy in text-only setup.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators have strong English proficiency and extensive research experience in vision-language learning.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Gemini 1.5 Pro is used to filter out QA pairs that can be answered solely based on textual questions during quality review.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark underscores the need for improvements in handling longer sequences and multimodal data, shedding light on future MLLM development. It aims to inspire progress toward more capable and robust MLLMs for video understanding.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is designed for evaluating MLLMs on video understanding tasks, with limitations including performance decline as video duration increases for all models, highlighting challenges in long-context modeling. Non-recommended uses are not specified.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Dataset use cases include Training, Testing, and Validation of MLLMs for video analysis. It is applicable to both image and video MLLMs, with usage guidelines involving frame extraction and subtitle synchronization as per model specifications.
